role: You are working in the daily-ai-pulse Astro codebase as a front-end implementer.
context:
Visual targets (priority over conflicting guidance elsewhere, except where "Known mismatches" says otherwise): docs/reference-layouts/images/about.webp, methodology.webp, subscribe.webp, contact.webp, privacy.webp, terms.webp. Responsive HTML references live next to them (about.html, methodology.html, subscribe.html, contact.html, privacy.html, terms.html) and are authoritative for structure; use them to resolve anything the images leave ambiguous. All six share one shell and differ only in the main column:
Shared shell (image sections S1-S3): S1. Global header: serif wordmark, nav (Today / Pulse / Categories / About), search affordance, black pill "Subscribe". Owned by BaseLayout; only verify that "About" is the active nav item on /about/ and that no nav item is active on the other five pages. Do NOT copy per-image header variations (a tagline beside the wordmark, a terracotta Subscribe button, vertical dividers); the images disagree with each other here. S2. Information sidebar (left, about 20-25% of the width): a vertical list About / Methodology / Subscribe / Contact / Privacy / Terms. The current page is terracotta, heavier weight, with a 3px terracotta bar on its left edge; other items are muted regular. A thin vertical rule separates the sidebar from the content (visible in methodology, subscribe, contact, privacy, terms; absent in about). Sidebar spacing is generous (about 3rem between items' baselines at desktop). S3. Page head in the content column: small-caps tracked terracotta eyebrow, very large black display-serif H1 on a single line at desktop width with tight tracking, then a muted serif dek (one to two lines). Left-aligned, no illustration, then a thin rule before the first section.
Per-page main column: - About: after the head, rows of "label | body" separated by thin rules. Left column is a small-caps tracked terracotta label (PURPOSE / THE EDITOR / EXPLORE), right column (about 65%) is a serif body paragraph with terracotta underlined inline links. Dek is larger (about 1.6rem) than on other pages. - Methodology: head has an extra bold-ish intro paragraph under the dek. Sections are two columns: a regular-weight serif section title on the left (about 1/3), content on the right. "Evidence levels" content is a term/definition table: bold serif term column, muted definition column, thin rule between rows. A final "Corrections" section. - Subscribe: numbered sections ("01", "02" in terracotta), each with a large serif title (RSS, Email), a paragraph, and a right-hand column separated by a thin vertical rule: a small-caps tracked "GOOD TO KNOW" label with a checkmark list in the RSS section, "ON THE ROADMAP" label with a short paragraph in the Email section. The RSS section has a dark pill button "Open the RSS feed" with an external-link icon and the feed URL in muted text beneath it. - Contact: sections "Corrections" and "Questions and feedback", each with a regular-weight serif h2, a paragraph, and (for Corrections) a dark rectangular button ("Open GitHub issues"). Thin rules between sections. - Privacy: three plain sections (serif h2 + muted paragraph), no rules between them, generous vertical rhythm. - Terms: three sections separated by thin rules; the last has a terracotta underlined inline link. Palette/type for all: warm beige canvas, black display serif for H1/h2, muted gray for dek/body, terracotta only for eyebrow, active sidebar item, labels/numerals, and inline links; --ink for buttons.
Known mismatches to resolve: - The images' text is generated and fabricated. Per IMAGE_GALLERY.md, do NOT copy it. Examples: "a small, independent team", "support independent coverage", "peer-reviewed research", "reputable technical media", "https://thedailyaipulse.com/rss", "Full articles, no paywall", "Works with any RSS reader", "We read every issue", "© 2024", "reader-supported publication", and the Terms claim that work may be shared with attribution under MIT. Every sentence must stay factually true for this project (single maintainer Alexandre Gadaix, GitHub issues for contact, RSS only, email planned but unavailable, GitHub Pages hosting, dual licensing in CONTENT_LICENSE.md and LICENSE). Keep the existing real copy as the source of truth and restructure it into the image's layout; only add a statement if you verify it in the repo (for example, check src/pages/rss.xml.ts before claiming "full articles"). - Headlines: the image H1s match existing ones for About, Methodology, Subscribe, and Contact. For Privacy and Terms, adopt "Privacy, plainly." and "Use and attribution." with the existing eyebrows replaced by "PRIVACY" and "TERMS", and write a one-line dek for each (do not use the image's dek if it overstates anything). The Terms "attribution" wording must match CONTENT_LICENSE.md exactly in substance; if the license does not grant sharing with attribution, say what it does grant and link to it. - The images show only a subset of each page. Keep every real section that exists today and is not in the image (Contact: "Security or private concerns"; Privacy: "Hosting"; Terms: "Full text"; About: "Who makes Pulse", AI-tool disclosure; Methodology: evidence-vs-signal note and the "← About Pulse" return link). Fit them into the same layout rather than deleting them. - Footer designs differ across the six images and from each other. The footer is owned by BaseLayout and out of scope; do not change it. - Image features not in the product: the copy-URL button (Subscribe), any email form, any contact form. Do not add them. Show the real feed URL as plain text built from Astro.site + import.meta.env.BASE_URL + "rss.xml". - The image shows populated pages only; there is no dynamic data here, so no empty/loading states are needed.
Current implementation (inspect before editing, do not redo): - Each page is src/pages/{about,methodology,subscribe,contact,privacy,terms}/ index.astro, wrapping an `` in BaseLayout. Shared styles live in src/styles/global.css (`.information-page` and `.primary-link`, max-width 800px, centered, h1 700 weight capped by `max-width: 12ch` in about, single-column sections with a top rule). - There is no sidebar and no shared information layout. Create one Astro layout or component (for example src/layouts/InformationLayout.astro wrapping BaseLayout, with props for title, description, eyebrow, heading, dek, and current page) so the six pages share the sidebar, grid, and head, and the page list lives in one place. Do not create six copies of the sidebar. - methodology/index.astro has scoped styles for `.evidence-list` (term/definition rows); reuse and tune them rather than rewriting. - No e2e test currently references these pages by content; the accessibility spec may crawl them, so axe must still pass.
task: Align the six information pages with their images section by section: introduce a shared information layout with the left sidebar (S2) and page head (S3), then restructure each page's main column to match its image using the real copy. Adjust global.css only for the shared `.information-page` rules that conflict with the new grid; put page-specific styles in the page's scoped `
constraints:
- Match column proportions, spacing, dividers, and type hierarchy as closely as the images show. H1 is a single line at desktop width (remove the `max-width: 12ch` and `
` in About; scale with clamp so it does not overflow at 1024px). Methodology/contact/privacy/terms h2 and Methodology section titles are regular weight serif, not 700; check the current 700 against the images. - Sidebar: a `nav` with aria-label "Information", a list of six links built from import.meta.env.BASE_URL, `aria-current="page"` on the current item in addition to the terracotta bar (no color-only distinction). One h1 per page; section titles are h2 in document order. - Label/body and term/definition structures use semantic markup: About rows as sections with an h2 styled as the small-caps label (not a div); evidence levels stay a `dl`; Subscribe numerals ("01") are aria-hidden and the h2 carries the name; the checkmark list is a `ul` with decorative aria-hidden check icons; the external-link icon on the RSS button is aria-hidden and the link text stays "Open the RSS feed". External GitHub links keep their current rel/target behavior. - Buttons ("Open the RSS feed", "Open GitHub issues") are links styled with --ink background, 44px+ tall, visible keyboard focus. Contact's button points to the existing issues URL; it must not claim "We read every issue" or any response commitment. - Reuse existing design tokens (--terracotta, --ink, --muted, --line, --surface, --canvas); do not introduce new colors. - Base path: all internal links and the feed URL go through import.meta.env.BASE_URL / Astro.site; no hard-coded root-relative paths. - Responsive: below tablet width (about 860px) the sidebar becomes a horizontally wrapping row of links above the head (keeping the active state), the vertical rule becomes a bottom rule, two-column section rows (About, Methodology, Subscribe) collapse to a single column with the label/title above the body, and the Subscribe right-hand column moves under the section content with a top rule. No horizontal overflow at 320px. - Meta titles/descriptions in each page's BaseLayout props stay accurate; if you change an H1, keep the title tag consistent with it. - Do not modify files under docs/reference-layouts/. Do not add features beyond the images (no forms, copy button, email capture, table of contents, or analytics). - Run npm run check, npm run lint, npm run format:check, npm run build, and the e2e accessibility spec (npx playwright test tests/e2e/accessibility.spec.ts); fix any failure you introduced.
output_format: Provide the edits as: the new shared information layout/component, the six page files, and the minimal global.css changes. After the edits, list which image section (S1-S3 plus the per-page structures) each change corresponds to, and call out the fabricated-text, kept-real-sections, footer/header variation, and unsupported-feature (copy button, forms) decisions explicitly. List every factual claim you added or changed and where you verified it in the repo.
